# What the requester has been told

The work recorded these decisions as taken on the requester's behalf and showed them to the requester.

1. (R-1) How do I change the hours?
   Decided: Set SLA_HOURS_URGENT, SLA_HOURS_HIGH, SLA_HOURS_NORMAL or SLA_HOURS_LOW to positive whole hours.
   Otherwise: Use a single JSON environment value.

2. (R-2) Is a ticket overdue exactly at its due time?
   Decided: It is overdue only after that instant.
   Otherwise: Count it at the exact instant as overdue.

3. (R-3) How do I prepare the data file?
   Decided: Run the one-shot backfill with the service stopped, then enable the feature. Enabled startup also fills missing dues before listening.
   Otherwise: Rely entirely on startup backfill.

4. (R-2) What happens with other overdue query values?
   Decided: Only the literal true activates the extra filter.
   Otherwise: Reject other values with 400.
specification:
# Help desk ticket service specification

## Requirements

### R-1 Assign a due time once

Basis: 2026-11-21 response-time request. New ticket due is its persisted created time plus 4 urgent, 24 high, 72 normal or 168 low elapsed hours. Default of 2026-11-21: use individual positive whole-hour SLA_HOURS_<PRIORITY> environment settings, with unset values using the defaults and invalid values naming the setting. A priority update, lifecycle change, config change, or feature toggle retains the assigned value. Verify with deterministic HTTP creates and a file-backed restart.

### R-2 Expose due times and filter overdue tickets

Basis: 2026-11-21 response-time request and docs/api.md listing contract. With DUE_TIMES=on, ticket reads, create, edit, transition and lists expose ISO due. Default of 2026-11-21: only literal overdue=true narrows a list, and overdue means open or in progress with a due instant strictly before now. Preserve the status/priority OR filter, sort, cursor and envelope. Verify equality, resolved and closed exclusions, and combined filters with loopback HTTP.

### R-3 Backfill before activation

Basis: 2026-11-21 response-time request and data-file decision 8. Fill absent dues from existing created and priority without modifying audit, outbox, ticket IDs, update times or assigned values. Default of 2026-11-21: use a one-shot offline command and catch up missing dues before enabled startup listens. Verify file read-back, repeated backfill, and restart with a changed policy. Off-mode API responses stay in the baseline shape and ignore overdue. The single service process or the offline operator owns the data file at any one time.

### R-4 Readability in rollback

Basis: 2026-11-21 response-time request. Actual 1.4.0 must start using the new file and list its existing and newly created tickets. Its writer discards the optional due field, so operator instructions preserve the due-bearing copy and protect later ticket changes during re-upgrade. Verify against a copy using the unchanged 1.4.0 executable.

### R-5 Preserve existing behavior and tests

Basis: 2026-11-21 response-time request and CONTRIBUTING.md. Preserve dependency-free Node 22+ service, npm start and PORT, CLI and raw report contracts, and the unchanged suite. Add node:test coverage under test/ and run npm test.

## Non-functional requirements

The version-1 file remains atomically replaced and single writer. Feature work adds no service, timer, dependency or new personal data. The existing CLI retains the documented table and raw contracts. No new graphical interface is introduced.

## Retired

None.

items.decision: Rollback uses the version-1 file with optional due fields that 1.4.0 strips on its next save, so operators are expected to keep a due-bearing copy and protect ticket changes made during rollback when upgrading again.
items.alternative: The requester might have expected original due times and all ticket changes to survive a writable rollback and re-upgrade automatically.

items.decision: The specification assigns and saves due times for new tickets even while DUE_TIMES is off, with the flag controlling what the HTTP API exposes.
items.alternative: The requester might have meant for tickets created while the flag is off to receive their first due time during backfill, under the policy and priority in effect then.

items.decision: Due times use continuous elapsed hours, including nights, weekends and holidays.
items.alternative: The requester might have meant for the promised hours to count only while the help desk is open.

items.decision: The overdue filter narrows the results of the current status-or-priority matching rule, so a ticket that is overdue can match just one of those two parameters.
items.alternative: The requester might have expected a combined query to require the ticket to match overdue, status and priority together, as the existing API documentation describes for its filters.

items.decision: Unset SLA hour overrides use the stated defaults, while an invalid override is treated as a configuration error that identifies the offending variable.
items.alternative: The requester might have preferred the service to start with the default for that priority and warn the operator about the invalid override.
